partition_policy.training: all target facts except source-exclusive validation and blind facts

results.name: Direct LOF protein-abundance restoration
results.hypothesis: A drug that directly binds a loss-of-function disease driver and increases its abundance may restore deficient protein dosage.
results.body: drug directly binds LOF Gene2Phenotype driver and causes increased driver abundance
results.mechanism_rationale: The rule directly opposes deficient protein dosage using an aspect-specific abundance effect on the causal driver.
results.trapi_notes: The binding, abundance-effect, and variant-qualified disease paths are TRAPI-expressible; provenance and ontology constraints require post-processing.
results.cypher:
MATCH (subject:Drug)-[:DIRECTLY_PHYSICALLY_INTERACTS_WITH]->(driver:Gene)
MATCH (subject)-[effect:AFFECTS]->(driver)
MATCH (driver)-[association:ASSOCIATED_WITH]->(object:Disease)
WHERE effect.qualified_predicate = 'biolink:causes'
  AND effect.object_aspect_qualifier = 'abundance'
  AND effect.object_direction_qualifier = 'increased'
  AND 'infores:gene2phenotype' IN
      coalesce(association.primary_knowledge_sources, [])
  AND association.subject_form_or_variant_qualifier = 'loss_of_function_variant_form'
  AND coalesce(object._miner_disease_descendant_degree, 0) <= 500
  AND object._miner_disease_superclass_degree >= 1
  AND object.id STARTS WITH 'MONDO:'
RETURN DISTINCT subject.id AS subject_id, object.id AS object_id

results.name: Direct LOF protein-abundance suppression control
results.hypothesis: Decreasing the abundance of a loss-of-function disease driver is a matched countermechanism control.
results.body: R295 with decreased rather than increased driver abundance
results.mechanism_rationale: The abundance effect worsens rather than corrects deficient protein dosage.
